end.summary:
Practised making one mark for each object to keep track without number names.
Matched marks to objects to identify an extra object or a missing match.
Parth correctly used one mark per object in 4 attempts and matched marks correctly in 4 of 5 attempts.
Explaining why one-to-one matching works remained unfinished.
Parth continued to think that spreading objects out makes the row contain more; this was not corrected by the end.
end.parentNote: Asha practised one-to-one matching with objects, marks, and examples such as stones for boats. Parth consistently used one mark for each object and noticed when a mark or object had no partner. A mix-up remained: a spread-out row still seemed to have more objects, and this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, place matching pairs of everyday objects in both a close row and a spread-out row, then check each pair one at a time.
